data.title: Columbus Circle Capital says Elroy Air wins up to $46M U.S. Army contract
data.description:
• Columbus Circle Capital (CMII) said Elroy Air was awarded a $46.1M firm-fixed-price U.S. Army contract to develop an autonomous hybrid-electric VTOL uncrewed aircraft system for modular multi-mission payload delivery.
  • The contract, awarded through Army Contracting Command, has an estimated completion date in 2029. About $5.1M in fiscal 2026 funds were obligated at the time of the award.
  • Elroy Air’s Chaparral drone is designed for autonomous heavy-cargo delivery, and the contract builds on prior Army agreements, the company said.

data.title: Two Harbors gets final regulatory approval for CrossCountry deal
data.description:
Two Harbors Investment (TWO) announced it received the final regulatory approval for its planned sale to CrossCountry Mortgage.

The deal is expected to close before the market opens on Tuesday, according to a statement on Friday.

TWO stockholders will be entitled to receive $12.00 per share in cash. In addition, TWO stockholders of record at the close of business on Aug. 24 will be entitled to receive a stub period dividend in an amount equal to $0.20326 per share of TWO common stock. The stub period dividend will be paid with the merger consideration and will not reduce or otherwise affect the merger consideration.

data.title: Applied Optoelectronics slips as it files for $600M equity distribution deal
data.description:
• Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) shares slipped more than 4% in extended trading on Friday as the optical component company filed for a $600M equity distribution deal.
  • The agreement was entered into with investment firms Raymond James and Needham, Applied said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: BIGG rebrands as Surge Digital, announces 7-for-1 share consolidation
data.description:
• BIGG Digital Assets (BIG:CA) plans to change its name to Surge Digital and its TSXV ticker from BIGG to SRGE.
  • The name, ticker and share-consolidation changes are expected to take effect on August 26, 2026.
  • The company will consolidate its common shares at a 7-for-1 ratio.
  • BIGG currently has 355.78M shares outstanding, which will fall to ~50.83M after consolidation.
  • Surge Digital will continue to own and operate Netcoins, Blockchain Intelligence Group and TerraZero.

data.title: Kairos Pharma announces 1-for-7 reverse stock split to maintain NYSE compliance
data.description:
• Kairos Pharma  (KAPA) announced on Friday that it will conduct a 1-for-7 reverse stock split effective September 1, 2026, before the market opens.
  • The company’s shares will continue trading on the NYSE American under the ticker KAPA.
  • Under the split, every 7 shares will be combined into 1 share, with fractional shares rounded up to the nearest whole share.
  • The reverse split will proportionately adjust the company’s convertible notes, warrants, and equity awards.
  • The company said the move is intended to increase its per-share trading price and help maintain compliance with NYSE American listing requirements.
  • On the market side, the shares traded over 7% lower at ~$0.27 in the after-hours trading session.

data.title: Global Interactive gets Nasdaq notice over delayed 10-Q
data.description:
• Global Interactive Technologies (GITS) announced on Friday that it received a Nasdaq notice over its delayed Q2 2026 Form 10-Q filing.
  • The company has 60 days to submit a plan to regain Nasdaq listing compliance.
  • If accepted, Nasdaq may allow the company until February 16, 2027, to regain compliance.
  • The company expects to file its Form 10-Q promptly, while its common stock will remain listed and traded on Nasdaq during the 60-day grace period, subject to other listing requirements.

data.title: Breeze Acquisition faces Nasdaq compliance issue over delayed Q1, Q2 filings
data.description:
• Breeze Acquisition (BREZ) announced on Friday that Nasdaq flagged the company for failing to file its Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Q reports on time.
  • The company has until September 21, 2026, to submit a plan to regain compliance.
  • If Nasdaq accepts the plan, the company could have until December 28, 2026, to resolve the filing issue.
  • The notice has no immediate impact on the company’s Nasdaq listing or trading.
  • Breeze Acquisition said it plans to take the necessary steps to regain compliance.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Nasdaq ends positive on broader rally, but tech stocks lead weekly losses
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed flat but in the green on Friday in tandem with other indexes on Wall Street, as Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fluctuated sharply as it extended a volatile rebound from below $64K earlier this week. The index ended at +0.43%.

Chip and AI-related stocks were largely mixed on the day.

For the week, the tech-focused index declined after ending in the red for three out of five sessions, dragged down by technology stocks. The top five detractors for the week ended August 21 saw a clear rotation between technology stocks, led by Nebius Group (NBIS).

The gainers showed a mix of stocks across several sectors and were led by Strategy (MSTR). The company  returned to a profit on its Bitcoin holdings, with an unrealized gain of roughly $1.4B, as the cryptocurrency advanced nearly 22% over five straight sessions, CoinDesk reported.

Top gainers of the week:

Strategy (MSTR) +28.17%

Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) +8.36%

Copart (CPRT) +6.93%

Marvell Technology (MRVL) +6.77%

CoreWeave (CRWV) -16.54%

Arm Holdings (ARM) -12.93%

Seagate Technology (STX) -12.68%

Intel (INTC) -12.13%

data.title: Calif. Governor Newsom prefers Warner Bros/Paramount settlement 'if it's a good deal'
data.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would like to see a settlement of the state attorneys general's lawsuit to block Paramount Skydance's (PSKY) $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) "if it's a good deal."

“That has to be worked through, and that’s a process that’s unfolding,” Newsom said Friday at a press conference in San Francisco, according to a Bloomberg account  of the event. “I’m concerned about the state, our reputation.”

Newsom's comments come after a WSJ report that Newsom was concerned about the state's suit to block the deal. Newsom is concerned that if the combination is blocked, it could have negative implications for employment in the state.  Newsom's office is encouraging Bonta's office to find a settlement outside of court. Newsom doesn't have any role in the litigation and doesn't have authority over the state AG's actions.

Earlier this month, Paramount (PSKY) CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the movie studio out of California if he couldn't reach a settlement with California's AG. Paramount (PSKY) would move the studio to Tennessee, Texas, Georgia, or another identified state if he can't reach a deal with California AG Rob Bonta by Oct. 1, according to a Puck News report. 

Newsom said at the press conference on Friday that he didn't think Paramount wanted to leave California, though he added that he was taking the possibility seriously.

“I hope that doesn’t happen, and I’m of the belief that they don’t want to see that happen,” Newsom said. “I’m talking about the future of the industry. I’m talking about Hollywood.”

On Wednesday, Cinemark  (CNK) became the latest movie theater chain to back the merger of Paramount (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), joining Regal Cinemas and AMC Theaters (AMC) in support of the deal.

Shares of Warner Bros. rose 1.1% on Friday, while Paramount edged higher by 0.7%.
